name: LHAASO (Daocheng): KM2A detectors and WCDA pools
notes: Drawn: the 1188 KM2A muon detectors (15 compact blocks of at most 80), the three WCDA pools, and the outline of the 5216-detector ED array. The map format has no multi-point type, so each muon detector is a 6 m square marker (the area-equivalent of its 36 m2) in a MultiPolygon. The 5216 electromagnetic detectors are NOT drawn one by one: as 1 m markers they need 26 000 vertices and push this map file to 3.5 MB, over the 2 MB size limit for a map file; their positions were read and checked and the outline carries the ED array.

Positions are read from the vector graphic of Fig. 1 of the LHAASO Science Book (Chin. Phys. C 46, 030001, CC BY 3.0; arXiv:1905.02773 v4, PDF page 8), registered to a second published copy of the layout (Fig. 1 of arXiv:2401.01038; 5215 of 5216 EDs within 2 m), and placed at the coordinate the Collaboration gives (29 21 27.56 N, 100 08 19.66 E). Checks: 4911 EDs inside 575 m and 305 outside (stated 4911 and 305), farthest ED 635.2 m (stated 635 m), pool sides 150.1 m, 150.1 m, 300.2 m x 110.1 m (stated 150, 150, 300 x 110), pool total 78,109 m2 (stated 78,000), ED hull span 1270.2 m (stated 1270 m).

The three pools are also traced in OpenStreetMap (ways 1046559931 to 1046559933, extract 2026-10-25T11:28:50Z) and lie within 1 to 3 m east and 2 to 10 m north of the placement used here, which supports the anchor; OpenStreetMap shapes are not used in any record (the OSM "Kilometer-Square Array" way 1003419124 is a regular 38-gon of radius 619.8 m centred 2 m from the coordinate, i.e. a drawn circle, not a trace).

Not drawn: the 18 WFCTA telescopes. The Science Book figure shows them as schematic 7 x 10 m rectangles at the junction of pools 1 and 2, but the text puts them "at the southwest corner of the first pool" and their container is 4.2 m x 2.5 m x 2.6 m; no position is taken from it.
It is not stated whether the layout shows design or as-built positions: the plotted EDs have a median nearest-neighbour distance of 13.6 m (stated spacing 15 m).

The previous version carried one 50 m-precision reference point (geometry:lhaaso-array-point) at the quoted coordinate; it is kept as the anchor marker. The 2016 and 2018 papers give 29 21 31 N, 100 08 15 E (164 m away); two 2020-2024 papers print "100.01 E" (a typo, about 12.5 km west).

summary.plain: The LHAASO cosmic-ray observatory on the Haizi Mountain plateau in Sichuan at 4410 m: the outline of its kilometre-wide disc of 5216 electromagnetic detectors, its 1188 muon detectors, and the three adjacent water Cherenkov ponds near the centre, all drawn to scale from the Collaboration’s published layout figure.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:lhaaso-daocheng. KM2A ED (5216) and MD (1188) positions and the three WCDA pool rectangles are read from Fig. 1 of the LHAASO Science Book (vector graphic), registered to a second published layout (arXiv:2401.01038), centred on the Collaboration’s coordinate 29 21 27.56 N, 100 08 19.66 E and oriented by the figure’s north arrow (accuracy 30 m; the pools agree with OpenStreetMap to 10 m). The MDs, the pools and the ED-array outline are drawn; the individual EDs and WFCTA are not.
